sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, rising from $404.5 million to $5.93 billion [F196][F1][F10].
The FY2017 operating margin of -422.5% [F22] was the window low [D553], driven by stock compensation rising to $2.64 billion [X82] on the CEO award and IPO-related RSUs [P74].
The FY2022 setback saw the operating loss grow 98.7% to $1.40 billion [D264][F17] as cost of revenue rose on revenue share and DAU-linked infrastructure [P48].
FY2025's -9.0% operating margin [F30] is the best in the window [D554], improving from -14.7% in FY2024 [F29].
Advertising supplied 5.3pp of the 10.6% FY2025 revenue growth [D538][D551] and remains 87.4% of revenue [D536].
Other Revenue grew 62.9% [D544] and added 5.4pp [D545], which the filing attributes to subscriber growth [P24].
Advertising grew 5.8% [D537] on more impressions, partly offset by a lower price per impression [P24].
Operating costs grew 5.1% [D423] against 10.6% revenue growth [D551], a 5.5pp gap [D430] and an incremental operating margin of 44.8% [D429].
Net loss shrank 34.0% [D408] and diluted loss per share shrank 35.7% [D410] as diluted shares rose 2.1% [D425].
Operating margin of -9.0% [F30] sits at the window high [D554], far above the window median of -32.4% [D555].
The FY2025 gain of 5.7pp [D419] came mainly from other operating lines (3.3pp [D433]), then R&D (1.3pp [D432]) and cost of revenue (1.1pp [D431]).
Sales and marketing expense fell to $1.02 billion [X50] from $1.06 billion [X49], which the filing ascribes to prior-year event timing and lower advertising spend [P22].
The largest move, FY2018's 315.1pp [D92], came mainly from other lines (+175.1pp [D105]) and R&D (+120.6pp [D104]), tied by the filing to lower stock compensation [P75].
Other income of $68.9 million [X130] lifted FY2025 net margin to -7.8% [F50] above operating margin of -9.0% [F30], mainly on debt extinguishment gains [P18].
Operating cash flow of $656 million [F80] exceeded a net loss of $460.5 million [F40] because stock compensation of $1.02 billion [X90] is non-cash [P13].
Free cash flow was $437 million [F100], a 7.4% margin [D393] at the window high [D560].
Capex of $219 million [F90] ran at 1.34x depreciation and amortization [D395], mainly leasehold improvements for team workspaces [P10].
Stock compensation was 155.0% of operating cash flow [D396], so cash generation leans on a non-cash cost that still dilutes shareholders.
Net cash was -10.1% of revenue, or net debt of $596 million [D400][D399], at the 0th percentile of five internet peers [D578] versus a peer median of 45.0% [D579].
Net cash has fallen four years running [R3], from $1.44 billion in FY2021 [D211] to net debt, after long-term debt grew 66.1% in FY2022 on new notes [D274][P41].
New notes funded repurchases of older notes [P2][P1], and long-term debt fell 3.3% in FY2025 [D417] to $3.49 billion [F185].
Buybacks of $751 million [X156] were 171.7% of FY2025 free cash flow [D402], yet diluted shares still rose 2.1% [D425].
Net losses have appeared in every year since FY2016 [R1], most recently $460.5 million in FY2025 [F40].
Stock compensation was 17.1% of FY2025 revenue [D390][R2], and diluted shares rose from 808 million in FY2016 [X141] to 1.69 billion [X150].
Interest expense rose to $122 million [X100] from $21.6 million [X99], driven by interest on the 2033 and 2034 notes [P19].
Operating margin holding above -9.0% [F30] in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the trend, while a slide back toward -14.7% [F29] would reverse it.
Net cash moving back above $197 million [D256] would reverse the debt trend, while net debt wider than $596 million [D399] would confirm it.
Buybacks plus dividends falling below FY2024's 142.3% of free cash flow [D354] would signal easing, while a rise above 171.7% [D402] would confirm the pressure.
